documents: Burschil, Buness & Schmelzbach (2022) Near Surface Geophysics 20, 331-348, published paper (PDF)

entry.evidence: to demonstrate the feasibility of shallow 3-D multicomponent S-wave surveying

steps.action: Set out to establish a shallow 3-D 6-C S-wave reflection survey capability, which they report has no published near-surface precedent.
steps.quote: to demonstrate the feasibility of shallow 3-D multicomponent S-wave surveying

steps.action: Posed two further aims: map the overdeepened-valley succession in high detail and explore the presence of anisotropy.
steps.quote: (3) to explore the presence of anisotropy

steps.action: Relied on the authors' earlier source tests, which showed that the ELVIS-VII micro-vibrator yields reflections from 200 m depth with frequencies up to 100 Hz.
steps.quote: we conducted source tests that showed that the small electrodynamic micro-vibrator ELVIS-VII

steps.action: Designed a symmetric orthogonal geometry from stated requirements: 1.5 m bins from the aliasing criterion, 9 m line spacing, sources restricted to active patches, and nine patches.
steps.quote: We chose a conservative value of b = 1.5 m

steps.action: Acquired 6-C data (two horizontal source orientations, 3-C geophones) over 117x99 m2 in ten days.
steps.quote: In February 2018, we carried out a 3-D survey using a 2-C source (two horizontal components) and 3-C receivers

steps.action: Inspected raw correlated gathers and found a strong 600 ms reflection on parallel components, faint on vertical, plus clipping noise and surface waves.
steps.quote: we identify a strong reflection at 600 ms two-way traveltime

steps.action: Compared day-dependent first-arrival time shifts with meteorological records (freezing and thawing) and attributed them to changes in near-surface S-wave velocity.
steps.quote: We assign these traveltime changes to weather-dependent ground conditions

steps.action: Adapted Alford-type four-component rotation into radial-transverse coordinates, using each source-receiver azimuth after balancing source gathers.
steps.quote: we, therefore, rotated the horizontal components from the acquisition geometry

steps.action: Checked the rotation against the unrotated data with traces, hodograms and gathers: energy focuses on SrRr and StRt, with faint remnants on the cross components.
steps.quote: Component rotation focuses energy on the two parallel components SrRr and StRt

steps.action: Checked the separated Rayleigh (320 m/s) and Love (340 m/s) surface-wave velocities against theoretical relations.
steps.quote: This conforms with the theoretical values

steps.action: Found that the earlier 2-D f-k filtering workflow failed on the irregular 3-D offset distribution, so introduced data regularization.
steps.quote: an irregular offset distribution that prevents an effective application of the f–k filter

steps.action: Tested two regularization approaches (CMP supergathers with differential NMO, and CRS partial stacking) and adopted CRS.
steps.quote: We tested two regularization approaches

steps.action: Tested several fan-filter passbands (and, per the Discussion, tau-p filtering) and selected the f-k reject window.
steps.quote: After testing different velocity (fan) filters, we rejected areas <−1000 m/s and >+500 m/s

steps.action: Ran separate stacking-velocity analyses for SV and SH; the models agreed within picking uncertainty, so StRt velocities were used for NMO of all components, and migration was skipped.
steps.quote: The two velocity models do not show significant differences considering the picking uncertainty

steps.action: Produced stacked sections showing the undulating 600 ms reflection and a shallow reflection package, with reduced coherence over patch 1.
steps.quote: The most prominent features of the stacked sections are the undulating 600 ms reflection

steps.action: Brought in the authors' earlier 2-D P-wave prestack depth-migrated profile, about 35 m away, for comparison.
steps.quote: Burschil et al. (2018) published five 2-D P-wave seismic reflection profiles.

steps.action: Depth-converted the volumes with a single velocity function, interpreted the seismic facies by the known succession, and mapped the basin-base horizon at 145-155 m.
steps.quote: Molasse (1) and waterlain till (2) appear as a prominent reflector at around 145–155 m depth

steps.action: Compared the SV and SH volumes as independent polarizations: the basin-base horizons and faint basin-fines reflectors agree, while the upper till differs.
steps.quote: The interpreted horizons in SV- and SH-wave show a great similarity

steps.action: Compared the S-wave images with the P-wave section: the S-wave images are clearer and higher resolution, image layers too shallow for P, and are consistent in eastward dip and depression.
steps.quote: The SV section appears even more coherent than the SH section, and both are clearer than the P-wave section.

steps.action: Reported that refraction statics failed and a decoupled static was not used; replaced them with elevation and residual statics computed on the entire dataset.
steps.quote: The application of refraction static corrections was not successful since first arrivals were not pickable

steps.action: Tested for anisotropy by comparing SV and SH NMO velocities; differences lie within the semblance uncertainty.
steps.quote: Therefore, we do not infer anisotropy from the presented data.

steps.action: Proposed rival explanations for the SV/SH difference in the till: reflection coefficients, radiation pattern, residual Rayleigh waves, and guided or refracted waves. None was tested.
steps.quote: a different spatial radiation pattern of the wave energy could be a reason for a different reflection signature

steps.action: Kept the claim that shallow 3-D 6-C S-wave surveying is feasible with moderate effort and exceeds the prior 2-D P-wave imaging, and gave recommendations.
steps.quote: We presented the first shallow small-scale 3-D multicomponent source and multicomponent-receiver S-wave investigation

tree.answer: Whether 3-D multicomponent S-wave reflection imaging works in shallow Quaternary sediments
Yes; reflections are observed directly in 6-C gathers and stacks
Demonstrate feasibility, map the basin succession, explore anisotropy
Rivals stated only post hoc, for the SV/SH difference in the till
No distinct predictions derived for the rivals
Conditions found in a single field survey; weather varied uncontrolled
Processing alternatives tested; SV and SH volumes agree at depth; consistent with the P-wave profile
Survey and processing strategy shown feasible; anisotropy not inferred

end.claim: A shallow 3-D 6-C S-wave survey with rotation and CRS regularization is feasible with moderate effort and images the Tannwald Basin base and infill at higher resolution than the prior 2-D P-wave data.

decisive_move.sentence: The 3-D processing strategy (azimuth-dependent radial-transverse rotation plus CRS regularization enabling f-k filtering) turned the raw 6-C data into separable SV and SH volumes; without it no S-wave images exist.

gates.evidence: Acquisition was directed by survey-design requirements (depth >140 m, aliasing-free, >=100x100 m2), not by a hypothesis. These requirements and the bin-size criterion were fixed before acquisition (p. 334). The feasibility claim could have failed (e.g. no usable reflections) and was checked against the P-wave profile. The anisotropy test was stated as an aim, but no threshold was fixed.

novelty_claims.quote: there are, to the best of our knowledge, no published reports on 3-D multicomponent seismic reflection surveys
we present the first 3-D S-wave reflection seismic dataset recorded in a glacially overdeepened Quaternary basin
We presented the first shallow small-scale 3-D multicomponent source and multicomponent-receiver S-wave investigation
The basin base is well mapped in three dimensions and shows undulations that were not obvious from the P-wave data.

limits: No review file was supplied, so the review sequence is not coded. Sub-claims: (1) basin-base depth map 145-155 m, estimate_with_resolution in form only, since no depth uncertainty or resolution figure is given; (2) faint reflectors within the basin fines, best_explanation, resting on SV/SH similarity; (3) anisotropy, no_conclusion, because differences are within semblance uncertainty; (4) the cause of the SV/SH difference in the upper till is untested, with rivals listed only and no exclusion; guided or refracted waves may contaminate this layer. Weather-induced time shifts were not fully corrected, and patch 1 data were disregarded in interpretation. There is no borehole or S-wave control at the site; the nearby P-wave profile is low quality there. Processing choices (fan-filter window, CRS over supergathers, tau-p rejected) appear to have been judged visually; no quantitative comparison is reported (inference). Migration was skipped. A detailed interpretation is deferred to a later paper.

disagreements.target: Burschil et al. (2018) 2-D P-wave imaging of the Tannwald Basin
disagreements.support: The S-wave volumes, 35 m from the P-wave profile, show basin-base undulations, faint basin-fines reflectors and shallow layers not resolved in the P-wave section.
disagreements.quote: Both types exceed the limits of the previous 2-D P-wave imaging.

disagreements.target: Burschil and Buness (2020) tailored 2-D S-wave processing with f-k filtering on equally spaced gathers
disagreements.support: Irregular offset distribution in 3-D CMP gathers prevents effective f-k filtering, so regularization by CRS had to be added to the workflow.
disagreements.quote: The offset sorted gathers of the 3-D data show an irregular offset distribution

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Any bin size below the 2 m aliasing limit

alternatives_considered.chosen: CRS partial stacking within offset bins
alternatives_considered.alternatives: CMP supergathers with differential NMO; increasing bin size; flex binning; interpolation
alternatives_considered.reason: it is able to respect the dip of the reflectors

alternatives_considered.chosen: Fan filter rejecting <-1000 m/s and >+500 m/s in the f-k domain
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Other velocity (fan) filter windows; tau-p domain filtering

alternatives_considered.chosen: StRt stacking velocities for NMO of all components
alternatives_considered.reason: the two velocity models do not differ significantly within picking uncertainty

alternatives_considered.chosen: No migration of the stacked volume
alternatives_considered.reason: avoid edge effects because of small volume size and lack of large dips

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Refraction static corrections; decoupled static correction
alternatives_considered.reason: first arrivals not pickable and irregular offsets; decoupled static would need time dependence and repeated installations

alternatives_considered.chosen: Interpret only SrRr and StRt components, excluding patch 1
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Including cross components and patch 1 data
alternatives_considered.reason: low-quality patch 1 data; faint reflections on cross components
